findings.title: code_drift reports `diverged` after an ordinary squash merge, so the SessionStart banner tells the reader 'this verdict describes different code' about byte-identical code - on this repository's own merge workflow
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/state.py:545-549: any non-zero return from `git merge-base --is-ancestor recorded HEAD` is reported as `diverged`. A squash merge creates a new commit, so the branch tip is legitimately not an ancestor

reproduced in a scratch repo modelling this exact workflow: state written on feat/x at 5cc9c3d4, PR squash-merged to main as dbbb1efd, then `code_drift(repo, '5cc9c3d4')` returned {'status': 'diverged', 'commits': None}
the code is identical while the banner says it is not: `git diff --stat main feat/x` reports 0 files differing, and both commits have the same tree 20a0b199c6c7098a1d7ec77aa0b5f5e229ea9775
the banner text that would print: 'Measured on a commit that is not in this branch's history - this verdict describes different code.' (hooks/report_open_findings.py:101-103)

this repo squash-merges: `git log --format='%h %p %s'` shows one parent per PR commit for #39 through #45 (0a9269a<-5a26ac0<-c04aedc<-021a27f...), and .qa/state.json is committed, so main will carry a branch sha that main's history does not contain
it fires on THIS PR: state written at 0a9269a on feat/commit-staleness; once squash-merged, every session opened on main sees the false divergence line until the next QA run
the fix direction is verified: comparing `git rev-parse <recorded>^{tree}` to `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` gives equal trees for the squash case and different trees for a genuinely diverged branch
secondary, same function: `merge-base --is-ancestor` returns 128 for a bad object and the code reads that as `diverged` too - measured exit 128 for a nonexistent sha

root_cause.symptom: a loud, wrong 'this verdict describes different code' on unchanged code
root_cause.mechanism: 'not an ancestor of HEAD' is treated as equivalent to 'different code'. Squash merge, rebase, cherry-pick and amend all break ancestry while preserving content, so ancestry alone cannot carry that meaning
root_cause.origin: introduced this range in 0a9269a (state.py:545-549), the commit that added code_drift
root_cause.class: the same modelling error is duplicated in prose: commands/status.md:24-25 instructs the agent 'the recorded commit is not in HEAD's history -> the verdict describes code this branch never had. Say that plainly.' An agent following that instruction makes the same false claim, so a code-only fix leaves half the defect alive
root_cause.latent_condition: tests/test_code_drift.py:61 and :126 both construct divergence with a side branch carrying DIFFERENT content. There is no negative test asking whether `diverged` fires when it should not, which is why a proven false positive shipped with 140 lines of new tests around it

findings.title: gate --require-harness is defeated by imitation, not just forgery: both durable signals are visible in the committed .qa/ artifacts a fabricating model would copy
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/state.py:364 DURABLE_SIGNALS = ('state_computed', 'report_rendered'); state.py:398 tests `isinstance(state.get('calibration'), dict)` and state.py:400 tests a fixed literal string in the report

defeated in two edits, measured: taking the scratch hand-written state that exited 6, adding `"calibration": {}` and appending the literal 'rendered from `state.json` by `verdict-finalize`' to the report flipped the gate to `VERDICT: pass -> exit 0`
an empty dict suffices - `isinstance({}, dict)` is True, so no field of calibration is inspected

the templates are in the repository, which is the point: `grep -c` finds the footer literal once in the committed .qa/reports/2026-08-30-re-baseline.md, and the committed .qa/state.json carries a `calibration` object with keys min_sample, findings_tracked, decided_outcomes...

so in team mode - the mode this repo uses and the README recommends - a model that fabricates a run by imitating the previous report and previous state reproduces both signals without ever intending to defeat anything
the docstring at state.py:357-363 is honest that the signals are weak; the user-facing framing is stronger - commands/run.md:47 'exit 6 - the state was hand-written'

root_cause.symptom: a fabricated run can pass the check that exists to catch fabricated runs
root_cause.mechanism: both signals are static, publicly-documented constants with no dependence on the measured values, so reproducing them requires no measurement
root_cause.origin: the durable-signal design in f516f73/state.py, chosen deliberately because facts.json is gitignored - the tradeoff is sound, the strength of the remaining signals is what is unaudited
root_cause.class: checked the two corroborating signals too (facts_measured, judgment_written): facts_measured at state.py:397 does bind to the run (`facts.get('measured_at') == stamp`), which is the stronger shape - it is simply not part of DURABLE_SIGNALS

findings.title: fixture_freshness reproduces the fixture lossily: content of tracked files only, so mode changes, symlink swaps and planted untracked files are invisible, and a missing tracked file tracebacks
evidence: all four probed in a purpose-built scratch git repo running the shipped eval/fixture_freshness.py unmodified

PROBE D (blind): an untracked, non-ignored file planted in the fixture dir ('HINT.md') -> gate exits 0, 'OK'. The eval feeds the fixture DIRECTORY to a model, so a planted file changes what the eval measures while the tamper gate reports clean; the old --no-index implementation caught this case
PROBE E (blind): `chmod +x` on a tracked fixture file -> gate exits 0 while raw `git diff --stat` reports the file changed. shutil.copyfile at eval/fixture_freshness.py:54 copies content, not mode
PROBE F (blind): a tracked file replaced by a symlink to identical content -> gate exits 0, while git reports 'mode change 100644 => 120000'

PROBE C (unclear failure): deleting a tracked fixture file -> raw traceback 'FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory' from shutil.copyfile at fixture_freshness.py:54. It exits non-zero so the tamper IS caught, but with a Python traceback instead of the designed message the file already has for its other failure mode (SystemExit at line 47)
PROBE G: a broken symlink in a tracked path produces the same traceback
controls confirming the gate still does its main job: PROBE A (ignored build artifact) -> correctly 0; PROBE B (genuine unstaged content edit) -> correctly 1
usability note from PROBE B: the failure message prints 'committed: 8 lines / regenerated: 8 lines' - two identical numbers, which is the wrong discriminator for the commonest tamper

root_cause.symptom: a tamper-evidence gate that reports OK on four kinds of tamper and tracebacks on a fifth
root_cause.mechanism: `git ls-files` + shutil.copyfile reconstructs only the content of tracked regular files; git's own notion of the fixture also includes mode and object type, and the eval's notion includes every file present on disk
root_cause.origin: introduced with the F-5 fix in c04aedc; the docstring at fixture_freshness.py:17-20 states the tracked-only choice but does not acknowledge what it stops seeing
root_cause.class: this is the F-9 shape recurring - a designed error path exists (SystemExit at line 47) but the adjacent failure raises raw. Same author, same range, different file
